proposals.expected_signal: Higher NDCG@10 if mild uniform message corruption reduces popularity-dominated co-occurrence and improves tail-item ranking without destabilizing top-item signals.
proposals.failure_mode: Uniform edge dropout may erase too much sparse-user signal in ML-1M, causing weaker item connectivity and lower ranking quality across both head and tail items.
proposals.hypothesis: Applying stochastic edge dropout only during light graph propagation with standard pairwise ranking will regularize over-smoothed collaborative signals and improve top-10 ranking.

proposals.expected_signal: Improved NDCG@10 if a contrastive auxiliary term sharpens user-item embedding geometry beyond what plain matrix factorization learns under pairwise supervision.
proposals.failure_mode: The auxiliary loss may dominate the recommendation objective, producing well-clustered embeddings that are not aligned with full-sort ranking quality.
proposals.hypothesis: Adding a lightweight contrastive auxiliary objective on top of latent-factor embeddings will increase representation separation for positives versus sampled negatives and improve ranking.

proposals.expected_signal: Higher NDCG@10 if learned mixing across propagation depths captures both local and higher-order preference structure better than fixed-depth aggregation.
proposals.failure_mode: Extra transformation capacity may overfit ML-1M or make optimization noisy, yielding no gain over simpler graph propagation baselines.
proposals.hypothesis: Introducing residual message transforms with learnable layer-wise aggregation under pairwise ranking will better balance shallow and deep collaborative evidence for top-k recommendation.

proposals.expected_signal: If NDCG@10 drops versus uniform-negative training, it indicates this pilot setting is sensitive to sampler-induced objective mismatch and benefits from keeping negatives simple.
proposals.failure_mode: The falsification may be inconclusive if the hard-negative heuristic is too weak, making results look similar to the uniform baseline without isolating the actual mechanism.
proposals.hypothesis: Replacing pure uniform pairwise ranking with a contrastive auxiliary term built from harder within-batch negatives will not help under the frozen ML-1M protocol and may expose over-concentration on ambiguous negatives.
